items.reason: Every exception list (7 SAST allowlist rules + the 4 ESLint fences, 14 measured rows) now carries a ceiling with a reason and a removal condition in .github/contract-ledger.json, and the previously-unwired scripts/contract-ledger.mjs --check now enforces it as a blocking stage of check:ci — a list that grows past its ceiling, or a new fence with an uncapped list, fails the pre-push gate.

The narrating subjects were not being Ack'd around (Ack: only unblocks A3/A4) — they were landing on a path with no hooks, and one family passed the rule outright; scripts/commit-subject.mjs now refuses the consulted-documents list, the run tally and the semicolon-joined report clause, pinned by a new test-unit/commit-subject.test.mjs, so A5 refuses them in check:ci and in agent-review.yml. The commit-time half (a committed .husky/commit-msg) could not be added: .husky is a protected path in this session.

Needs network: all 23 refs are first-party actions on version tags and pinning them means asking GitHub what each tag points at right now (scripts/actions-pin.mjs --update, which also flips STRICT/RATCHET in the same pass); inventing a SHA breaks the workflow rather than pinning it.

The runbook already exists and says so itself — docs/runbooks/revert-drill.md, 'Status: never run', with the seeds, the stamps and the promotion rule for when it becomes a gate; what is missing is a RUN, which needs a shell and a deploy this session has neither of.

Needs a test runner: a mutation score is produced by running the suite once per injected fault, and this session has no node_modules and no ability to execute anything — a harness written blind and never run is exactly the unverified artefact the brief refuses.

Needs signing/attestation infrastructure and git: making the run→commit link verifiable rather than declarative means attesting the commit the way CI attests artifacts, and the in-tree alternative (staging .agent/checkpoints/<session>.json into the same commit) cannot work under this repo's mandatory pathspec commits, which ignore index additions made by a hook.

lessons: This repository ships tooling faster than it wires it: scripts/contract-ledger.mjs and .github/contract-ledger.json landed with a $comment claiming they were 'blocking inside check:ci' while package.json defined no such script and nothing referenced the file. Before writing a new gate here, grep package.json and .husky for the one that already exists — the gap is usually the wiring, not the idea.

Autopilot lanes commit from a throwaway worktree with no node_modules and no .husky/_, so no git hook in this repo fires on the commits that most often break its rules. Any guardrail meant to reach agent-written commits has to hold over a RANGE at push time (rubric A5 / check:ci), not at commit time.

Gate rungs here are chosen by measurement (ADR-0007): a check goes on the blocking rung only if it passes on the tree the day it lands. A ratchet or ceiling set to today's count is the way to make an unbounded thing blocking immediately, and the repo prefers that over a new reporting-rung script nobody reads.
